#2727. Giants' J.J. McCarthy returns against Eagles after hip injury sent QB to locker room

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The New York Giants appear to have survived another injury scare at the quarterback position. J.J. McCarthy returned to Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles after spending time in the sideline medical tent and locker room while being evaluated for a hip injury.

With McCarthy initially deemed questionable to return, the Giants turned back to Jameis Winston, who started four games before McCarthy replaced him atop the depth chart. Winston led a touchdown drive before he headed back to the sideline.

McCarthy took a hard hit to his lower abdomen on a quarterback keeper in the third quarter. Eagles linebacker Zack Baun led with his helmet while attempting to stop McCarthy's run and made contact with McCarthy's side on the tackle.

JJ McCarthy has checked out of the game and into the blue tent after taking this hit to his throwing shoulder pic.twitter.com/UusCnXfBos

McCarthy attempted to throw on the sideline before heading to the locker room and was in obvious pain after he completed his throwing motion. He grabbed at his side and fell to the turf as medical staff came to his assistance. Despite the clear discomfort, he was able to get back into game action just before the end of the quarter.

J.J. McCarthy is in pain after an apparent injury.📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/qP3JfP2PUn

The Giants were mostly quiet on offense during McCarthy's Week 9 start and scored only six points before he left with the injury. McCarthy was 9-for-13 for 101 passing yards and ran three times for another 11 yards ahead of his brief exit.

Although it seems that McCarthy will remain in action beyond this week, if the injury acts up on him and forces him to miss time, his potential absence may be a significant blow to the NFC East-leading Giants. Already without Jaxson Dart for the rest of the year due to the torn knee ligaments he suffered in Week 2, New York traded for McCarthy as a potential season-long solution. His effectiveness upon insertion into the lineup in the fourth quarter of the Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints and in his first start the following week came as a pleasant surprise and gave the Giants reason to believe they could maintain their division lead.

Winston has been serviceable in his own right, so perhaps the Giants could stay afloat if they are ever forced to hand the keys back to him. He went 2-1-1 in his four starts before McCarthy replaced him, and that stretch included a 326-yard performance in the tie with the Washington Commanders and a 250-yard outburst the previous week in a victorious effort. Winston's lack of consistency has long been a limiting factor in his ability to command an offense as a starter, however.

#2726. MLB Power Rankings: Brewers end 2026 season at No. 1 as World Series champions

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

I'm done. No more. Enough is enough. I have doubted the Brewers far too many times and I decided in early August to never do it again. I started picking them to win the World Series every chance I got. I was finally right.

Every time they traded away someone good (the latest being Freddy Peralta last offseason), I thought, "OK, now is when it finally catches up with them." Only it never does. I thought they needed Tarik Skubal, both to reinforce their rotation and also to keep him away from the Dodgers. It didn't matter. They beat him and swept the Dodgers in the NLCS.

It's a juggernaut of an organization. They churn out talent and get the most out of every player they have. They seem to trade away talent at the exact right time. They develop young stars better than anyone. There's another one coming in Jesús Made, but there's no reason for Brewers fans to dream about the future when the present is World Series champions.

Jackson Chourio is becoming a superstar, Jacob Misiorowski is going to win the National League Cy Young and Christian Yelich is a former MVP, but it isn't really about the big names with this group. It's everything. It's the entire team making this train run, working as a cohesive unit. It's Robert Gasser going out and dealing in Game 3 after starting the season in the minors. It's Jake Bauers winning NLCS MVP not too long after he was ready to retire from baseball. It's Aaron Ashby putting up one of the greatest reliever performances in playoff history. It's Sal Frelick hitting a game-tying bomb. It's Cooper Pratt's coming-out party in the World Series. And on and on and on we could go.

Milwaukee is the best organization in baseball now, supplanting the former two-time defending champion Dodgers.

The Brewers head to next season with plenty of question marks, but they'll answer them. They always do. They are the champions of Major League Baseball and they sit atop the final 2026 Power Rankings.

Looking forward to next spring, my expectation is the Brewers will be No. 1. Some years, I write about why the defending champion is not No. 1. I've long since learned my lesson with this team, though. No more. The Brewers will be No. 1 heading into spring training.

Milwaukee continues its quest for the second World Series appearance in franchise history when it hosts Yoshinobu Yamamoto and the Dodgers at 5 p.m. ET in Game 2 of the 2026 NLCS at American Family Field. The Brewers, who were swept by Los Angeles in this round last year, made their only trip to the Fall Classic in 1982 and lost to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games while residing in the American League.

The Dodgers took the lead in Game 1 on Andy Pages' RBI single in the second inning, but Brice Turang led off the fourth against Skubal with his second career postseason homer and Luis Lara put the Brewers ahead in the following frame with a run-scoring base hit. It proved to be enough for Milwaukee as relievers Abner Uribe, Aaron Ashby and Trevor Megill kept Los Angeles off the board over the final four innings.

Owners of the best record in the major leagues during the regular season (103-59), the Brewers now must solve Yamamoto, who is 8-1 with a 2.14 ERA in 11 playoff games -- 10 starts -- since joining the Dodgers in 2024. The 28-year-old Japanese right-hander has allowed fewer than two runs in eight of his 11 overall postseason appearances and seven of the last eight.

Yamamoto went 5-1 with a 1.45 ERA and two complete games in last year's playoffs and was named World Series MVP after recording three victories against the Toronto Blue Jays. One of those complete games came in Game 2 of the 2025 NLCS, as he limited the Brewers to three hits and one run while registering seven strikeouts. Yamamoto was dominant in his debut this postseason, holding the Atlanta Braves to one run and four hits while fanning 10 batters over seven innings in Game 3 of their NL Division Series.

Milwaukee counters with rookie Logan Henderson, who made his first career playoff appearance in Game 2 of the 2026 NLDS against the San Diego Padres and allowed two runs -- one earned -- and two hits across five innings of a no-decision. The 24-year-old righty won both of his starts versus the Dodgers during the regular season, permitting one run and five hits with 13 strikeouts over 12 innings. Yamamoto was effective against the Brewers this year, as well, going 2-0 while giving up two runs and fanning 12 across 13 frames in two outings.

The 2026 ALCS begins Monday as the Cleveland Guardians visit Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. to take on the Tampa Bay Rays at 8 p.m. ET. Left-hander Foster Griffin makes the start for Cleveland, which lost the first two games of the ALDS at home before posting three consecutive victories over the Chicago White Sox.

Tampa Bay turns to righty Drew Rasmussen, who was four outs away from a no-hitter in Game 1 of the Rays' three-game sweep of the New York Yankees in the ALDS and finished with 10 strikeouts across eight scoreless innings. Griffin did not face Tampa Bay this season, while Rasmussen went 1-1 with a 1.50 ERA and fanned 15 over 12 frames in two starts against the Guardians.

#2724. Russell Westbrook number retirement: OKC Thunder to hang No. 0 from the rafters in February

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Oklahoma City Thunder will put Russell Westbrook's No. 0 into the rafters at the Paycom Center on Feb. 7, 2027, when they host the New York Knicks, the team announced on Monday.

0 Forever 💙02.07.27 pic.twitter.com/pTqRnespU2

Westbrook retired this offseason after an 18-year career that saw him make nine All-Star teams, nine All-NBA teams and win the 2016-17 MVP award. All but one of those All-Star and All-NBA seasons came as a member of the Thunder; he averaged 23.0 points, 8.4 assists, 7.0 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game across 821 appearances in an Oklahoma City uniform.

"Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy. Russell Westbrook's legacy was built both on the court and in the community," general manager Sam Presti said in a statement. "His mindset was relentless, his commitment deep. For all those reasons, Oklahomans consider him one of their own and his number will be raised to the rafters, in Oklahoma City forever."

The Thunder traded Westbrook to the Houston Rockets before the 2019-20 season, but he struggled to stick with a team for long. While he remained productive, he bounced from Houston to Washington to Los Angeles (both the Lakers and Clippers) to Denver to Sacramento before calling it a career, never lasting two full seasons in the same place.

After a rash of injuries in Oklahoma City and with Westbrook's retirement still fresh, some wondered if the Thunder might consider calling in Westbrook for reinforcements on the roster. When asked about that possibility following Jalen Williams' season-ending injury and Cason Wallace's shoulder surgery, Presti insisted he hadn't considered any roster moves at that time.

"I haven't thought about anything relative to the roster spot," Presti said during a press conference last week. "I understand the question, but all I'm really focused on right now is players, getting them the right support, and then helping everybody with our group realize that, you know, we have a tremendous challenge in front of us."

From a basketball perspective, the fit between Westbrook and this current Thunder roster would've perhaps been a bit clunky, but many wondered if OKC still might pursue it as a fitting, emotional send-off for the franchise's favorite son. With the announcement of his jersey retirement, that puts to rest any speculation he'll end his retirement to return to play for the Thunder. Still, he'll get to return to the only team he ever called home long-term -- and the only fan base that ever truly embraced him.

"Let Westbrook be Westbrook" was a favorite saying during his prime years in Oklahoma City, and it's the only place he ever was able to do just that. After Kevin Durant left for the Warriors, Westbrook became the avatar of loyalty in OKC, and the Thunder faithful latched onto their star guard even more after feeling betrayed by Durant.

While it didn't yield the championship Westbrook and Thunder fans hoped for during his tenure, he is the most beloved figure in franchise history for what he did to establish NBA basketball in Oklahoma City and give back to the community. On Feb. 7, he'll get a chance to receive a long-awaited warm welcome back to his adopted home and see the No. 0 get raised to the rafters.

#2723. 10 NFL trades that need to happen: Derrick Henry to Patriots, Budda Baker to Bills among options

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The NFL trade deadline is just two days away, and it's already been a dramatic time around the league. The Seattle Seahawks beefed up their offensive line with Quenton Nelson, the San Francisco 49ers brought back DeForest Buckner, the Chicago Bears look like a Super Bowl favorite with the addition of Jeffery Simmons, and the Baltimore Ravens have a new quarterback in Jacoby Brissett. Who is the next domino to fall?

A total of 27 players were traded in-season last year. That's the most in the past 25 years. A total of 12 players were dealt on deadline day last year. Get ready for a wild 48 hours. There's a lot of speculation around Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, but will he actually get dealt? What about the Minnesota Vikings? Could they swing a deal for a new quarterback in the next 48 hours? Below, we will break down 10 trades that need to happen.

Vikings receive: QB Kirk CousinsRaiders receive: Conditional fifth-round pick

ESPN's Adam Schefter got a lot of people excited last week when he said he was going to keep an eye on the Vikings. Are they going to trade for Justin Herbert? Or Mac Jones? Maybe Daniel Jones? What about bringing back Kirk Cousins?

It doesn't appear that Cousins will be dealt at the trade deadline, but it would be a storybook ending if Kevin O'Connell brought Cousins back to town and he contributed to a Super Bowl run. Cousins spent six seasons in Minnesota, threw for 4,000 yards four times and went 50-37-1 as the starter. While he's 38 now, Cousins is still capable of playing good football. His 19 passing touchdowns entering Sunday ranked second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow, and his 265.5 passing yards per game ranked seventh.

Now that we are halfway through the 2026 season, the Raiders can turn their attention to No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, while Cousins will improve a Vikings passing attack that's sputtering. Kyler Murray's 170.3 passing yards per game entering Week 9 ranked 30th among 31 qualifying passers, and we don't know if Carson Wentz is a solution. Justin Jefferson is sick of not having consistent play under center, so let's get Cousins back to Minnesota and watch him power a Super Bowl run.

Bills receive: S Budda BakerCardinals receive: Third-round pick

How long can the Bills keep winning track meets? Josh Allen can outscore just about any team, but this defense ranks bottom 10 in both yards allowed per game (352.1) and points allowed per game (25.9). Buffalo has four wins in games the defense has allowed 30 points!

Adding Cardinals safety Budda Baker should help. He's an eight-time Pro Bowler playing great football for a not-so-great team. In eight games this season, he's recorded 51 tackles, four passes defensed, one interception and a career-high 3.5 sacks. Not many players have made 1,000 tackles before age 30 — just Bobby Wagner, Roquan Smith, Luke Kuechly, Lavonte David, Ray Lewis, Fred Warner and Budda Baker.

Patriots receive: RB Derrick HenryRavens receive: Third-round pick

Mike Vrabel has a few former Titans on his roster, including A.J. Brown and Kevin Byard. He could swing a deal for another one of his former players in Derrick Henry.

The Ravens running back is averaging 76.6 rushing yards per game and has scored nine total touchdowns in nine games played. Given the injuries at the quarterback position and the fact that the Ravens are the only team in the division with a losing record, it looks like Baltimore won't be making its Super Bowl run this year. Henry is 32 going on 33 and should be helping a contender.

The Patriots rank 12th in rushing yards per game with 123.1, but Rhamondre Stevenson is averaging under four yards per attempt and about 46 yards per game. TreVeyon Henderson's situation remains unclear as well, after he revealed he experienced an "unusual medical emergency." Vrabel knows what Henry is capable of as a bell cow, and he can help the reigning AFC champs get back to the "Big Game."

Raiders receive: WR George PickensCowboys receive: Second-round pick

George Pickens ranked third in the NFL in receiving yards last season with 1,429 and nine touchdowns on 93 receptions, but this season has been a different story. His yards per game has dipped from 84.1 to 66.6, and Pickens played just 56.8% of snaps during the Cowboys' Week 8 loss to Arizona.

Pickens is playing on the franchise tag this year and is due a massive contract. Questions remain about the Cowboys' ability to pay him. Dak Prescott is the No. 2 highest-paid quarterback in the NFL, CeeDee Lamb is the No. 6 highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL and Tyler Smith is the No. 2 highest-paid guard in the league. Then, the recently added Joey Porter Jr. is due a massive contract as well. Is Dallas really going to pay Pickens around $35 million per year? It makes sense to pick up a second-round pick for a player who may not be on your roster next year.

The Raiders, on the other hand, have one of the worst wide receiver rooms in the NFL.Tre Tucker leads the way with 474 yards, then Jalen Nailor is behind him with 113 yards. Pickens would provide Fernando Mendoza with a true perimeter threat for years to come.

Broncos receive: RB Breece HallJets receive: Third-round pick

Breece Hall signed a three-year, $43.5 million deal this offseason after being slapped with the franchise tag. He became the Jets' first 1,000-yard rusher since 2015 and is one of three active players to record 3,000 rushing yards and 1,500 receiving yards in his first four seasons. However, Hall's quad injury opened the door for Braelon Allen, who has really taken advantage of his opportunity. He rushed for a career-high 147 yards against the Raiders last week.

The Broncos' rushing offense entered Sunday ranked seventh-worst in the NFL. While rookie Jonah Coleman has flashed in spots and the injured RJ Harvey is a weapon as a receiver out of the backfield, Hall would immediately upgrade an inconsistent offense that has legitimate Super Bowl aspirations.

Chiefs receive: WR Josh DownsColts receive: Conditional fourth-round pick

The Chiefs would like Brian Thomas Jr., but they don't want to give up a second-round pick for a player with some question marks. They instead trade a conditional fourth-round pick for Josh Downs, who has recorded the second-most receiving yards out of the slot ever since he was selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of North Carolina.

Downs caught 30 passes for 330 yards and one touchdown in his first eight games this season and put up a career-high 803 yards and five trips to the end zone in 2024. The Chiefs' issues at wide receiver are well-documented. Rashee Rice entered Sunday averaging 48.6 receiving yards per game, and Xavier Worthy is just a gadget player at this point. Travis Kelce shouldn't be leading this team in receiving.

Steelers receive: WR Ladd McConkey, fifth-round pickChargers receive: WR Roman Wilson, second-round pick

CBS Sports' Bryan DeArdo pitched this trade earlier this week, and it makes some sense. Ladd McConkey could take the Steelers' passing attack to another level, while former Michigan head coach Jim Harbaugh would reunite with Roman Wilson.

McConkey has caught just 17 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown through the first eight weeks of the season. As a rookie, he caught 82 passes for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns. The Steelers have averaged 26.2 points per game over their last six, but their leading receiver, DK Metcalf, is averaging just 47.3 yards per game. In McConkey, Aaron Rodgers would get a solid slot weapon who could also act as a security blanket.

Giants receive: RB Tony PollardTitans receive: Fourth-round pick

Jonathan Taylor has gotten a lot of oxygen over the past few weeks, but there's another running back in the AFC South that teams should be interested in. Tony Pollard rushed for 129 yards and three touchdowns against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 and then 117 yards and two touchdowns against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. He's averaging a career-high 74.4 rushing yards per game this season, and he ranks top 10 in rushing attempts, rushing yards and rushing touchdowns. He and Derrick Henry are the only players to have rushed for 1,000 yards in each of the last four seasons.

The Giants do have Cam Skattebo, who rushed for 124 yards and a touchdown in that overtime win against the Houston Texans, but Pollard would upgrade a questionable room as New York looks to win the division. John Harbaugh was upset his team couldn't land Jeffery Simmons. Mike Borgonzi finally answers the phone and sends Pollard to the Giants.

Jaguars receive: DT Moro OjomoEagles receive: Third-round pick

The Jaguars have reportedly been sniffing around for defensive linemen, and Moro Ojomo could be a fit. Jacksonville just saw DaVon Hamilton go down with a torn quad, and GM James Gladstone hopes to make an addition to maintain one of the best run defenses in the NFL. Ojomo adds some juice as a pass rusher from the interior and has recorded the second-most pressures on the Eagles over the last three seasons behind Jalen Carter.

49ers receive: EDGE Khalil Mack, sixth-round pickChargers receive: Third-round pick

Reports indicate that Khalil Mack won't be traded, but this is a player who should be rushing the passer for a contender. The former Defensive Player of the Year turns 36 in a few months, but he can still get after the quarterback. Mack recorded three sacks in his first seven games this season and notched a career-high 17 sacks just three years ago.

The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (142) entering Sunday. The defensive line has 47 games missed by players, the most in the NFL. Mack would help a Raheem Morris defense that can win a Super Bowl if healthy.

#2720. Steelers 2026 mid-season awards: Who is Pittsburgh’s MVP?

We have reached the mid-season point of the 2026 NFL regular season (it always goes by too fast). The Pittsburgh Steelers have been one of the top teams in the league through nine weeks, sitting at the top of the AFC North with a 6-2 record while holding the No. 4 seed in the AFC playoff picture.

Over the course of this week, our staff here at Behind the Steel Curtain will roll out our mid-season awards, which begins today with the Steelers' 2026 mid-season MVP.

Joey Bray – RB Jaylen Warren: This award simply cannot go to anyone else. Warren was third in the NFL in scrimmage yards through eight weeks of play, and remains in fifth after the bye week. Plus, he is doing so with incredible efficiency. On an offense that lacks weapons on the outside, Warren is the engine that has the Steelers' offense on an upward trend heading into the second half of their season.

Austin Bechtold – RB Jaylen Warren: Warren entered the bye week with more rushing yards than Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor. His 6.93 yards per touch this season is the highest in football and 1.31 yards higher than the next closest running back (Bijan Robinson). Warren is the best weapon in the Steelers arsenal and has been revolutionary for an offense that has been relatively stagnant for half a decade. I'd be happy with Warren receiving additional carries, as long as his body can hold up. Warren seems like the obvious answer, but I think T.J Watt and Jalen Ramsey also have case.

Ryan Parish – C Zach Frazier: It was tempting to put Jaylen Warren here, but Frazier is so crucial to what Warren and the rest of the offense do, he has to get the nod. He's also the Steeler with the best case at being the best at his position in the entire NFL.

Ryland Bickley – C Zach Frazier: I'm torn between Frazier and Jaylen Warren here, but will go with the star center as he's been arguably the best at his position in the entire league this year. And hey, when it's a toss-up like this, why not give the offensive line some much-needed credit? Frazier has anchored the group that's been the story of the team's season thus far.

Mike Nicastro – RB Jaylen Warren: This one could certainly be up for debate, but my vote goes to Jaylen Warren. Warren has been the igniter of Pittsburgh's offense and arguably the biggest reason the Steelers are sitting at 6-2. Whether it's creating explosive plays, keeping the offense ahead of the chains or providing a spark when the passing game struggles, Warren has consistently delivered. Through eight games, Warren has rushed for 704 yards on 119 carries, averaging an impressive 5.9 yards per attempt. He's also added 294 receiving yards on 25 receptions, giving him 998 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Warren has become the engine of this offense. While there are other deserving candidates, it's difficult to overlook the impact he's had on a team that has won four consecutive games.

Jarrett Bailey – RB Jaylen Warren: It looks like I'm the tie-breaker here, but I'm going with Warren. Even after the bye week, he's fifth in the NFL in scrimmage yards and has emerged as one of the game's three-five best running backs. Without his productivity, there is zero chance the Steelers are 6-2.

#2719. Why Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg was benched after being 'peer pressured' into chasing 40 against Clippers

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has been a revelation to open his NBA career. Through his first seven games, he's putting up historic numbers, and he somehow keeps one-upping himself. On Sunday, he played his best game yet: 37 points on 85% true shooting. He made six of his 11 3-pointers and added six assists. He was outrageously good, as he has been all season, save for the Lakers game last Friday in which he was properly hazed by Luka Dončić.

Other than that, it's been nothing but buckets for Lendeborg, who, given how easily all this has seemingly come for him, perhaps got a little ahead of himself by chasing the 40-point round number on Sunday with a couple of, shall we say, questionable shots at the end.

Steve Kerr saw it, and with 2:14 to play, he benched his rookie as the Clippers were starting to make a desperate run, cutting a 21-point Warriors lead to eight over a two-minute span during which Lendeborg missed three 3-pointers, two of which were total chuck jobs.

"He would've had 40 if we had just kept playing [normally]," Kerr said after the game. "The NBA game these days can change like that. We all know that. Almost every night, there's a 25-point lead that is overcome.

"The game changed when all the guys on the bench were yelling at Yax to get 40. He launched three kind of bad shots. A lesson is, if you just keep playing, then you stay in rhythm, you stay in flow, the ball moves, and then the game becomes much easier. I think that's the lesson for him and for our team.

"But everybody loves Yax. Everybody wanted him to get 40. They were urging him to shoot from the bench, and It got us out of rhythm a little bit."

As soon as Lendeborg went to the bench and the Warriors got back to business, De'Antony Melton, who was a stud all night, buried back-to-back 3s to put the game back on ice. It was a great night for the Warriors, who've won four straight after opening 0-3, and for Lendeborg, who continues to be a total open book who is more than willing to admit to his mistakes and vow not to repeat them, as he did after the Lakers debacle when he took full accountability for "wetting the bed."

Yaxel Lendeborg was chasing 40 points late and it let the Clippers back into it briefly. He said he fell into peer pressure. It was his lesson of the night: "I've never been a stat chaser...I'm a guy that loves ethical hoops."Full Yaxel + Steve Kerr soundbite pic.twitter.com/5Lyo3CVXMb

"I've never been a stat chaser in my life," Yaxel said after he was benched on Sunday. "So, I mean, just falling into peer pressure like I did just now was pretty much bad on my part. Especially just, I'm a guy that loves, like, ethical hoops. I'm a guy that loves efficient basketball, and I didn't do that for the last two to three minutes. So, it's kind of, like, bad on my part. Next time I definitely won't do that again. If it comes to me, it does. If I don't get it, then I wasn't meant to get it that day. So, I'm gonna be way better next time."

Lendeborg elaborated on the peer pressure aspect of the chase, which, frankly, anyone can understand. You're a rookie and you're going off and your teammates are all cheering you on to keep shooting. The game, you think, is in the bag. Any player in that situation would've let a few more shots go.

"De'Anthony Melton went up to me and said, 'Hey, man you need to get 40. You're three points away,'" Lendeborg said. "And I'm like, 'Nah, It's all good.' He just peer pressured me into doing it. ... He said he's gonna give me the ball, and he literally was holding it just to give me the ball. I'm like, all right, fine, I'll shoot it,' and I missed. I tried to tell him 'no, no, no,' and now Will [Richards] came over [to me saying], 'you gotta do it, you gotta do it.'

"So everybody was just egging me on and I kind of just fell into it. But I know next time I'm just going to play in the flow of the game, because [the Clippers] came down and made like four threes in a row and we almost lost the game because of that. So next time I'm never doing that again."

#2717. Tarik Skubal landing spots: Predicting new home for two-time Cy Young winner, the offseason's best free agent

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Arguably the best pitcher in baseball is up for grabs this winter. Tarik Skubal is a free agent for the 2026-27 MLB offseason, easily the top available on the market, and every team should be trying to earn his services. But will they? Almost certainly not.

The 29-year-old southpaw spent the first six years of his major-league career with the Detroit Tigers before being traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the 2026 deadline. He won back-to-back Cy Young awards in 2024 and 2025 and earned MVP votes in both seasons. He's likely to become the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history both in total value and AAV.

Of course, the giant flashing sign floating above all of this is the expiring CBA, which will run out at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, after which the owners are expected to lock out the players until a new deal is reached. Over the summer, the league proposed limiting free agency contracts, an offer that the players' union quickly disavowed, and the owners' demand for a salary cap is the underlying throughline of every negotiation. Perhaps that means Skubal will rush to sign on the dotted line before new rules are in place. Perhaps that means teams will wait out the negotiations until they know how much they have to spend -- and how they'll be punished if they do so.

Regardless, CBS Sports' MLB experts, three people who are very much not involved in contract negotiations, have gathered to predict where Skubal lands by the time Opening Day rolls around.

Mike Axisa: I'll go off the board a bit and say the Padres. The new ownership group didn't pay $3.9 billion for the franchise only to cheap out in their first offseason. They're moneyed and motivated, and that's usually enough to land the top free agents. It should appeal to Skubal too. The Padres are in the postseason most years, they play in a great (and largely pitcher-friendly) ballpark, and it's San Diego. How can you not love San Diego? Skubal to the Padres because the new owners want to make a big splash in their first offseason. That's my prediction.

Dayn Perry: I'll say the Mets top all offers by a margin sufficient to overcome their lack of appeal compared to the usual suspects (meaning, mostly, the Dodgers). They definitely need a stabilizing force in the rotation outside of Nolan McLean, and they also need a vibes shift after the deeply disappointing 2026 campaign. Landing the biggest fish of all on the market would provide all that and meet a clear need. The Mets will already be rebound candidates in 2027, and signing the likes of Skubal would position them as contenders. Obviously, the structure of the next CBA has bearing here, but maybe this all comes together before the lockout shuts it all down for an indeterminate period of time.

Matt Snyder: I'll go with the easy and obvious answer and say the Dodgers. I don't think the owners win the fight for a salary cap, but there'll be enough push from the Dodgers' end before the CBA talks shut down free agency to snatch up all the talent they can to get his contract grandfathered before a new agreement.

#2715. Five things we learned from Victor Wembanyama's '60 Minutes' interview, including why he loves going barefoot

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

It is increasingly rare in the NBA (and professional sports as a whole) for a star athlete to sit down for an extended, on-the-record interview. While athletes have found other means of communicating with fans, such interviews can offer rare, less-filtered glimpses into what the player is going through both on and off the court.

Few players in any sport can say they've had a more eventful last few years than Victor Wembanyama. The San Antonio Spurs star reached his first NBA Finals last season and, in the process became a villain to fans across the world rooting for the New York Knicks to end their 53-year championship drought. He ultimately fell short in that matchup, but is now ascending to his seemingly inevitable place as the future face of the NBA. With the 2026-27 season only just beginning, Wembanyama sat down with CBS News' "60 Minutes" to discuss his career thus far. Here are five highlights:

Sponsorships are a standard component of the superstar experience. Wembanyama has been intentionally choosy about who and what he has aligned himself with. In the past, he has made it clear that he would never work with a soda company, for instance, because he does not want to promote unhealthy products. In Sunday's interview, he took aim at athletes promoting different vices.

"I think as an NBA player, and if you're amongst the stars of this league, you really make your career whatever you want to make it," he said. "Of course, you're always going to do your best on the court, the best that you can. But on the side, you can choose to be the influencer, you can choose to be the philanthropist, you can choose to be the guy who's gonna promote gambling and alcohol. You can choose whatever you want."

When asked what choice he has made, Wembanyama reiterated that health is his guiding principle. "I think my choice isn't final because I'm still growing as a person," he said. "But I want to promote healthy things, and by healthy, I don't just mean the food, but healthy habits, things that make people's lives better. And in the future, things that also make society better."

The public perception of Wembanyama changed quite a bit over the course of a single postseason. He was one of the league's breakout stars last season, and his consistent success over the widely disliked Oklahoma City Thunder earned him quite a bit of admiration from casual fans. However, his hard fouls, first in the second round against the Minnesota Timberwolves, and then later, of course, against the Knicks, turned him into a villain overnight. While Wembanyama claimed he wasn't paying attention to that noise during the Finals, he did learn from it after the fact.

"It showed my limits more than anything else," Wembanyama said. "Going out there, you need to play basketball, you don't need to beat the shit out of people. If you want to win at least." Had the Finals lasted beyond five games, he might have learned the lesson in more convincing fashion.

In Game 5, Wembanyama committed a foul on Jalen Brunson that many argued was flagrant after the fact, but because the Knicks ended the series then and there, the NBA was not forced to review it. Wembanyama was just one flagrant foul point away from a suspension for a hypothetical Game 6 at Madison Square Garden. Now, Wembanyama wants to make sure he doesn't put himself in that situation again.

Shoes are perhaps the single most important piece of equipment in a basketball player's arsenal, yet whenever possible, Wembanyama prefers not to wear them. "I try to walk barefoot as much as I can, and wear minimalistic shoes," he explained. For him, it's a matter of health.

"Because big men have always had feet problems," Wembanyama said, alluding to the NBA's lengthy history of injury-prone centers. "I also find more and more that feet are responsible for so much more that goes on. It's funny because I was just talking to a rookie. I went to practice barefoot and he sees me walk in without shoes and he goes, 'I did not know you could just not wear shoes.'"

Wembanyama believes that "if you've got good foot strength, which brings a good foot posture, everything else can level up the right way. Knee, hip, back and everything." Thus far, his methods seem to be working. His longest absence in the NBA came as the result of a blood clot in his shoulder, and while he has dealt with some of the same lower body injuries that many players are enduring in the pace-and-space era, he managed to maintain awards eligibility in both his first and third seasons. He has not yet missed a game this year.

Wembanyama has lived in the United States for more than three years now, yet he acknowledges how atypical his American existence has been. "When they ask me what it's like to live in the U.S., my answer is always, well, I don't know. I don't live a normal life in the U.S.," he said. "I live the life of an athlete, a rich person, the life of somebody that's gonna have everything taken care of no matter what I do, really. It's not the life of a regular American. It's the best country to be an athlete in."

That atypical experience has given him a unique perspective on life in the United States, and he sees both pros and cons compared to what he grew up with in France. "Good is how it feels like you're never judged for being ambitious," he argued. "Bad, I would say, I think the social interactions are more shallow here. Not as in-depth as they are in other countries."

Wembanyama is hardly the first foreign-born star to thrive in the NBA, but he's on pace to outshine all those who came before him. The NBA has obviously had plenty of international MVPs and champions, but it has never had a foreign face. Eventually, Wembanyama is expected to stand alone atop the sport, once the old guard of legends like LeBron James and Stephen Curry retire. That puts him in a somewhat unique position to attempt to influence the way stars conduct themselves moving forward. He is already seemingly attempting to do that in the way he chooses sponsors, and only time will tell how much more of his perspective will trickle down to his NBA contemporaries.

Wembanyama has never been shy about how excited he was to land with the Spurs. He called it "a winner's franchise," and cited both the team's history with French players and the presence of "the greatest coach of all time" as draws even before San Antonio won the 2023 NBA Draft Lottery. While that coach, Gregg Popovich, has since retired after suffering a stroke, Wembanyama got to start his career with Popovich on the sideline, and he explained that his greatest lesson was "about humility."

"He often said something when we were in film: after a win, you're rarely as good as you thought you were. And after a loss, you're rarely as bad as you thought you were," Wembanyama said.

That is a lesson that will have to persist this season, as the Spurs attempt to pick up the pieces following their Finals loss to New York. San Antonio blew double-digit leads in all four of its losses in that series, and the film will inevitably showcase many of the ways in which they were deficient against the Knicks. But the Spurs got to the Finals in the first place, well ahead of schedule, and while they should internalize what didn't work, they should hold onto what did.

It certainly seems as though they've done that this season, winning four straight after losing their first two games of the season. The Spurs are currently the championship favorite following a rash of injuries to the Thunder, and maintaining an even keel across the season will be essential in ensuring that they maintain that favored status.

Bangladesh veteran Mushfiqur Rahim added another landmark to his illustrious career, becoming the first batter from the country to score 7,000 runs in Test cricket. The 39-year-old achieved the milestone in the ongoing second Test against West Indies in Sylhet, further cementing his place among Bangladesh's greatest players in the longest format.Mushfiqur reached the landmark when he took a single off West Indies spinner Roston Chase to move to nine runs in his innings. The veteran initially appeared unaware of the achievement, but acknowledged the moment after his teammates rose from their seats in the dressing room to applaud him.The milestone was another reward for Mushfiqur's remarkable longevity and consistency in Test cricket. He had missed the opening Test of the series because of a finger injury but returned for the second match to add another chapter to his career.

Mushfiqur had already established himself as Bangladesh's leading Test run-scorer when he became the country's first batter to reach 5,000 runs in 2022 and 6,000 in 2024. He has now taken that record to another level, becoming the first Bangladesh player to breach the 7,000-run mark.He has accumulated 7,000 runs in his 107th Test, having needed only 25 innings to progress from 6,000 to 7,000. His tally includes 14 centuries, with his highest score being an unbeaten 219.Mominul Haque is second on Bangladesh's all-time Test run-scoring list with 5,293 runs, while former opener Tamim Iqbal is third. Mominul has scored 13 Test centuries, while Tamim has registered 10.Mushfiqur's latest achievement comes in a match in which his record for the highest individual score by a Bangladesh batter in Tests was surpassed. Towhid Hridoy struck an unbeaten 242 earlier in the ongoing Sylhet Test, going past Mushfiqur's previous best of 219 not out.

Having made his international debut in 2005, Mushfiqur is Bangladesh's most experienced Test cricketer. He became the first player from the country to feature in 100 Tests in November 2025 and is now appearing in his 107th match.His journey in the format has been one of steady evolution. Initially a lower-middle-order batter and wicketkeeper, Mushfiqur took 20 Tests to reach his first 1,000 runs. His batting responsibilities grew as he became a more established member of the side, particularly after taking over as Bangladesh captain in 2011.Over the years, he developed into one of the team's most dependable batters, producing crucial runs across conditions and against different opponents. His ability to maintain consistency over such a long career has been reflected in the latest milestone.

Mushfiqur has also made significant contributions in limited-overs cricket, scoring 6,697 runs in ODIs and 1,495 in T20 Internationals. He has since retired from both formats, with Test cricket remaining the stage on which he continues to extend his legacy.

#2710. Three notable decisions from NBA's rookie-scale extension deadline: Thunder seemingly give up on lottery pick

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Normally, the NBA's deadline for teams to pick up team options on their rookie-scale contracts is Halloween. As the end of October came on a weekend this year, however, it was pushed to Monday. This deadline is usually relatively uneventful. Former first-round picks living up to expectations, or with obvious paths to improvement in the near future, have their third- and fourth-year options picked up. Obvious busts tend not to.

Of course, teams inevitably get these decisions wrong from time to time, and that sends promising players to unrestricted free agency at the end of the season in question. The most notable recent example came in 2021, when the Phoenix Suns declined their third-year option on Jalen Smith, whom they'd selected at No. 10 overall ahead of players like Devin Vassell and Tyrese Haliburton less than a year earlier. Smith has since grown into one of the NBA's better shooting big men for the Chicago Bulls.

I bring this up because a handful of notable team options were declined ahead of Monday's deadline, setting some interesting prospects up for unrestricted free agency next summer. The NBA is more financially cautious than it has ever been thanks to the aprons, forcing teams to make hard decisions on young players before their futures are fully written. There will inevitably be more Jalen Smiths in the years to come, and a few declined options from the past few days stand out as candidates.

There's a degree of validation that comes with being drafted by the Oklahoma City Thunder. Sam Presti thought Nikola Topić was worth the No. 12 overall pick in 2024, and while Presti is hardly infallible, he's the NBA's best general manager by a wide margin and his instincts are usually worth imitation. Oklahoma City didn't decline Topić's 2027-28 option because he's played poorly. They declined it because he's barely played at all.

He missed his rookie season with a torn ACL. He missed most of his second getting treated for testicular cancer, only appearing briefly in 10 games. He has not yet played this season because of back surgery. It is entirely possible that Topić simply never stays healthy enough to reach his potential as a player. It is also entirely possible, especially on a Thunder team that suddenly needs minutes wherever they can find them, that he starts living up to that potential the moment he returns to floor.

Oklahoma City's injuries represent the greatest opportunity of Topić's career. The team that drafted him averaged 66 wins in his first two seasons. There weren't going to be many minutes available for him anyway. Now, if he can just make it back onto the court, he should get real on-ball reps for the team with the best player-development track record in basketball. He can set himself up for a real opportunity in unrestricted free agency next summer.

The Thunder were never going to be able to afford him long-term considering all of their other obligations, so in that sense, they've arguably done Topić a favor. If they'd picked up his option and then cap dumped him later, he might have wound up in a bad basketball situation. Now, he has the rest of the season to show what he can do and the freedom to shop his services to the teams that need them most.

Guard minutes were readily available for the Utah Jazz over the last two seasons. Isaiah Collier took plenty of them, averaging over 25 minutes per game in each of his first two seasons. Even with Darryn Peterson in the fold this year and Ace Bailey taking on a bigger role next to Keyonte George, Collier has still been featured pretty heavily by backup standards. Case in point: through six games, he is averaging the most minutes on the roster (18.5) of anyone who has not yet started a game.

Yet the Jazz surprisingly decided to decline his option for the 2027-28 campaign on Monday. What this means for the Jazz next season still isn't clear. Utah still has plenty of room below next season's projected luxury tax, but that space could evaporate quickly if they elect to re-sign restricted free agent Brice Sensabaugh and/or use a mid-level exception. Perhaps the Jazz want to seek out a veteran backup. They may also prefer to minimize their investment in ball-handlers to ensure that both George and Peterson play on the ball when the other rests. The Jazz have plenty of shot-creation in the front court. They can afford to be stingy at backup point guard.

Collier arrived in the NBA as a high-level playmaker. His scoring and defense just haven't kept up. But he was once the No. 1 recruit in his high school class, and there's plenty of tape on him already for other teams to study. The talent is here even if the role potentially wouldn't have been in Utah.

Tidjane Salaün was the highest draft 2024 Draft pick (No. 6 overall) to have his fourth-year option declined, but that probably works in favor of a potential reunion between him and the Charlotte Hornets over the summer if both sides want to pursue one. When a player has a rookie-scale option declined, his original team can still re-sign him in free agency ... but only up to the salary he would have made on that option. Salaün's fourth-year salary would have been $10.4 million or so.

That's a much heftier figure than later picks, and it creates a bit of a win-win scenario for the Hornets. If Salaün doesn't live up to that figure, they aren't forced to pay it to him and could try to keep him at a lower rate. If he does, however, then they are at least getting a productive player at a scarce position for this season. If nothing else, that's a valuable trade chip at the deadline.

Salaün's overall minutes have gone down in each of his NBA seasons thus far, but he's playing better than he ever has in that smaller role this year. That's not saying all that much, but his combination of physical traits, theoretical ball-handling and shooting and willingness to play hard at least offer the outline of a useful, all-around wing. This is a player archetype that teams are usually eager to take chances on. Whether it's with Charlotte or somebody else, Salaün will probably get another chance.

#2709. NFL trade deadline 2026: Ranking 20 players who could have the biggest impact if dealt

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The NFL trade deadline is on our doorstep. General managers and front-office personnel now need to take a hard look at their franchise and ask themselves what's best at this pivotal milestone. Do they hold firm, feeling like what they've put together is suitable for the rest of the stretch run? Do they sell after an uninspired start that has no reprieve in sight, shifting the focus beyond 2026? Do they buy, hoping that move could springboard them to glory? Those are the discussions happening right now.

Let's play in the buyer's sandbox for this discussion. No deal is equal. Some could simply be to add depth, while others are a swing-for-the-fences move, similar to what we've already seen from Chicago, when they shipped two first-rounders for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Below are 20 players who've been spinning in the rumor mill, ranked by the impact they could make if dealt to a new team.

Potential landing spots: Packers, Patriots, Broncos

After Philadelphia dropped to 2-7 with a loss to the Giants, everything should be on the table. That includes moving on from Pro Bowl guard Landon Dickerson, who has been among the Eagles players reportedly mulled over in trade talks. Philadelphia's offensive line has already seen big shakeups with Lane Johnson retiring and Cam Jurgens traded. It's possible Howie Roseman continues to gain future draft capital amid a lost season. While a guard doesn't exactly move the needle in terms of making headlines, Dickerson could be a true game changer for a playoff hopeful that needs help on the interior. That said, the 28-year-old has struggled this season. On top of missing time due to injury, Dickerson has allowed a sack in each of his four games played this season, so there is some risk for any team acquiring him. Meanwhile, Philadelphia could look to move on from Dickerson, with his cap number rising to $13.7 million and $17.7 million over the final two years of his contract.

Potential landing spots: Chiefs, Commanders, Rams

Jeudy isn't as high-profile a name as some other wideouts on the trade block, but he's still a quality pass catcher that could help deepen a room. This season, Jeudy has been buried on the Browns depth chart behind rookie Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, but flashed when his number is called. He's signed through 2027 with a base salary of just $1.5 million, so he'd be a cheap piece that could help a team for the stretch run of 2026 and beyond if they'd like.

Potential landing spots: Lions, Bills, Panthers

Woolen is playing on a one-year, $15 million contract. With free agency looming, he'd be a natural trade chip as Philadelphia sits at 2-7 as the deadline arrives. The 27-year-old corner is allowing a 51% completion rate when targeted this season, along with a career-high 99.9 passer rating. While the four touchdowns allowed isn't great, Woolen is a quality corner, which has plenty of value on the trade market. He also had a 73.6 passer rating allowed last season in Seattle, so there is the possibility that a change of scenery helps bring his production back to that level. Teams are always searching for help in the secondary, and if Woolen has the ceiling, to help be a steady piece for the stretch run.

Potential landing spots: Vikings, Giants, Broncos

Pollard isn't in the same tier as the likes of Jonathan Taylor or Derrick Henry. That said, the Titans back has been balling out in recent weeks leading up to Tennessee's Week 9 bye. Over his past two games alone, Pollard has rushed for 246 yards on a 5.3 yards-per-carry average to go along with five rushing touchdowns. The 29-year-old also caught six of his eight targets over that stretch for 46 yards. While he won't rush for over 100 yards in every game he plays down the stretch, he'd be an underrated addition for a team that is looking for a boost to its rushing attack. He's also set to be a free agent at the end of this season, so he may not cost as much as some other backs rumored to be available given his rental status.

Potential landing spots: Cowboys, Patriots, Packers

With the Chargers season already upside down, he'd be a fascinating addition for any team looking to bolster its pass rush. After all, the 2023 second-round pick recorded 13 sacks in 2025. He's only 24 years old, so he'd likely be hard to pry out of Los Angeles. However, Tuipulotu will be a free agent at the end of this season. If the Chargers don't have any plans to re-sign him, it'd be a logical move to see what they can get for him.

Potential landing spots: Broncos, Vikings, Seahawks

The veteran tight end is a solid pass catcher. Goedert signed a one-year, $7 million contract extension with the Eagles back in March and is set to be a free agent at the end of the season. If they can get more for him now than the compensatory selection they'll eventually receive if he signs elsewhere, it'd be a solid move for Howie Roseman. Goedert is also no stranger to playing on the big stage, suiting up in 13 playoff games over the course of his career and catching 56 balls for 595 yards and five touchdowns.

Potential landing spots: Bengals, Vikings, Giants

The Jets have been adamant that they won't move Hall before the deadline, but many will still inquire. That's especially true after the Week 9 loss to Kansas City that dropped them to 2-7 on the season. In that defeat, Hall led the team with 15 carries and rushed for 61 yards. That 4.1 yards-per-carry average was mirrored by fellow back Braelon Allen, who finished with 33 yards on eight carries. When Hall was sidelined the previous five games with an injury, Allen shined in the starting role, which should make Hall expendable at the right price. While Hall is more of a luxury piece on New York's roster, he'd be a bellcow back on most other rosters and could be the missing piece for contenders that are looking for some backfield help.

Potential landing spots: Bills, Commanders

Hooker has been putting together a career year with Tennessee so far. The veteran safety has five interceptions through seven games, which already ties his career high. He's also on pace to set career marks in total tackles and pass breakups. Before the bye week, Hooker showed his worth to a secondary with a three-interception performance against Joe Burrow and the Bengals in Week 8. Through seven games, he's allowed a 71.3 passer rating against. Hooker, a fourth-round pick in 2019, may be one of the more underrated pieces at the deadline, but his playmaking ability shouldn't be overlooked. His knack for creating turnovers could prove to be huge for a playoff contender. The only thing that may hamper his trade market is his contract, as he's under team control through 2028, but his cap hits are $13.1 million and $16.3 million over the next two seasons. Strictly looking at his play, however, he's a playmaker.

Potential landing spots: Chiefs, Patriots, 49ers

Downs has requested a trade out of Indianapolis, so he could be one of the names that actually gets moved before the deadline. The 2023 third-round pick out of UNC started to break out with an 803-yard sophomore season in 2024, but has quite made the leap most hoped he would to this point. Of course, part of that has been due to the Colts' continued issues at quarterback. He's shown the ability to create separation, and if he ends up on a team with better play under center, Downs could finally reach his ceiling. He's also set to be a free agent at the end of this season, so he may not cost much as a rental, making him attractive to a slew of receiver-needy teams.

Potential landing spots: Cowboys, Packers, Bills

Sweat logged 12 sacks for the Cardinals in 2025, so he's shown a strong ability to disrupt the quarterback. Pass rushers are always going to be a sought-after piece at the deadline, and with Arizona under .500, it'd made sense for them to deal away Sweat before Tuesday. That's especially true considering he has no guaranteed money remaining on his contract (that runs through 2028) beyond this season. That means Sweat will likely seek a revised contract. Inking a soon-to-be 30-year-old pass rusher doesn't seem like the most pressing need for a still-rebuilding Cardinals squad. Sweat is also no stranger to playing in big games, notably recording 2.5 sacks in Philadelphia's win over the Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX.

Baker is signed through 2027 and will turn 31 in January. With Arizona sitting in last place in their division, it makes sense that this would be a player they'd look to move for future draft capital at the deadline. Baker would be a fascinating addition to any defense as he's such a versatile weapon. The safety can play deep as well as near the line of scrimmage and is good against the run. He's a four-time All-Pro, but has only played in one playoff game in his career. Landing with a playoff contender and making a postseason run could spark the veteran.

Potential landing spots: Chiefs, 49ers, Raiders

Thomas looked like he was going to be the latest LSU receiver to take the league by storm with his 1,200-yard rookie season in 2024. Since then, however, the former first-round pick has fallen off dramatically and has been at the center of trade rumors this cycle. That's especially after he played just 19 snaps in Jacksonville's Week 9 win over the Ravens. While Thomas's production has fallen, he's still only 24 years old, and we've seen him dominate in the NFL before. It's possible he simply needs a change of scenery to tap back into that rookie version of himself. If he does and lands with a team like Kansas City or San Francisco, he could help shift the balance of power in the Super Bowl race.

Potential landing spots: Bears, Bills, Cowboys

Los Angeles is going nowhere fast in 2026 as they sit in last place in the AFC West, which makes any veteran -- especially someone like Mack -- subject to a slew of trade rumors. The Chargers have reportedly been unwilling to engage in trade talks despite their lackluster start to the season, but reality needs to set in at some point. Mack is much more valuable to them as a trade chip than an edge defender on the field, especially as he's on a one-year deal. A team acquiring Mack would get a future Hall of Fame talent that is still able to pressure the quarterback in what could be the final chapter of his career.

Potential landing spots: Vikings, Seahawks

Jones' name appearing in the rumor mill was a bit of a surprise, seeing as the Colts signed him to a two-year, $88 million extension. However, they should be exploring all of their options amid a 2-7 start and the recent firing of GM Chris Ballard. If they can get something for him and get out from under his contract, it could be a worthwhile endeavor. While Jones hasn't been able to recapture his magic from the first half of last season, he could be a solid option for a team like the Minnesota Vikings, who are dealing with an injury to Kyler Murray. Jones has familiarity with the organization as he spent time with them in 2024. If he ended up with Minnesota, he'd be one of the biggest wild cards of the second half of the season.

Potential landing spots: Patriots, Vikings, Giants

Baltimore is reportedly not expected to trade Henry before Tuesday's deadline, but his name has been in rumors. After all, the Ravens are last in the AFC North following their loss to the Jaguars, which dropped them to 4-5 on the season. The trade for Jacoby Brissett, alongside the hope that Lamar Jackson (fractured right thumb) could return late in the year, suggests they won't sell at the deadline, but it's not out of the realm of possibility they get a Godfather offer for Henry and have a serious conversation about moving him. Henry is set to turn 33 in January and is signed through 2027, but has no guaranteed money left on his deal beyond 2026. He could be more valuable to the franchise as a trade chip, and he'd be a remarkable addition to an RB-needy playoff contender for the stretch run.

Potential landing spots: Broncos, Vikings, Bengals

It does seem like the Eagles will listen to most players on the roster, but they're reportedly not looking to deal Barkley. Again, maybe that's simply because the right offer hasn't come across Howie Roseman's desk yet. Barkley is set to turn 30 years old this offseason, and injuries have started to pile up for the veteran back, so it'd make sense if they explored moving him, especially if they are on the verge of a reset following this 2026 season. Barkley would be one of the biggest midseason additions this cycle and, if he can stay healthy, completely changes the dynamic of how teams would defend whichever offense he'd end up on.

Potential landing spots: Chiefs, Raiders, 49ers

Wilson missed New York's Week 9 loss to the Chiefs due to a concussion, so teams looking to deal for him would have to be comfortable with his status going forward. That said, Wilson is one of the most underrated receivers in the NFL and would become a superstar if he fell in the right situation. Despite having lackluster QB play throughout his career, Wilson has three 1,000-yard seasons under his belt. He'd be a No. 1 option in most offenses and take any unit he'd land with to a new level. The question is whether or not the Jets would actually move Wilson. Despite plenty of speculation, they're reportedly not interested in dealing him. That said, if a team comes to them with a massive offer, at 2-7, they'd have to consider it.

Potential landing spots: Cowboys, Lions, Bills

The Raiders already traded Crosby once -- dealing him to the Ravens this offseason before the trade was nullified due to his physical -- so they could absolutely trade him again. Crosby is one of the league's top pass rushers and would be an all-in move for any team pulling off a blockbuster to trade for him. He won't come cheap, but Crosby is a disruptive force off the edge, which is immensely valuable come the postseason. The 29-year-old -- who is signed through 2028 -- dramatically improves any defense.

Potential landing spots: Vikings, Broncos, Bengals

Taylor didn't exactly make an exclamation point in Indy's Week 9 loss to the Cowboys to convince teams to go out and trade for him. He rushed for just 46 yards on 13 carries, while catching five of his six targets for 18 yards. That said, we all know that Taylor is one of the best backs in the NFL when he's firing on all cylinders. The Colts are about to hit the full reset button this offseason after falling flat with a 2-7 record so far in 2027. Taylor no longer fits their timeline and is better served as a trade chip to get assets rather than compete in the current moment. Taylor is a complete back who could have a Christian McCaffrey-like impact, whether he was traded to the 49ers or to whichever team can acquire him.

Potential landing spots: Vikings, Seahawks

The Raiders have reportedly not received any calls about Cousins, nor are they interested in trading him. I wouldn't be surprised if that changed, however, with teams at least checking in on his availability before Tuesday's deadline. Las Vegas has Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft, waiting in the wings. The club has been diligent in his development, but they'll have to turn the keys over to him at some point. If they believe that he's ready, it makes sense to ship out Cousins for future assets. If they do come to that realization, Cousins landing with a team like the Vikings -- whom he played for from 2018 to 2023 -- it'd flip the NFC North on its head. He'd be an upgrade over Kyler Murray -- who is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring injury -- and complement the best defense in the NFL. Minnesota would be taken even more seriously as a Super Bowl threat.

#2708. Contemporary Baseball Era Committee unveils eight Hall of Fame candidates: Dusty Baker, Bruce Bochy, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The National Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown on Monday announced eight candidates for election on the 2027 Contemporary Baseball Era Committee ballot. The non-player ballot includes four former managers and four former executives: Sandy Alderson, Dusty Baker, Bruce Bochy, Joe Maddon, Lou Piniella, Brian Sabean, Ted Turner, and Bill White.

The non-player ballot includes managers, executives, and umpires. On an alternating basis, the Era Committee also evaluates a ballot consisting of former players. As for the qualifications and criteria, the Hall of Fame describes it thus:

"The eight Contemporary Baseball Era finalists were selected by the BBWAA-appointed Historical Overview Committee from all eligible candidates among managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980. Eligible candidates include managers and umpires with 10 or more major league seasons and retired for at least five years (candidates who are 65 years or older are eligible six months following retirement); and executives retired for at least five years (active executives 70 years or older are eligible for consideration regardless of the position they hold in an organization and regardless of whether their body of work has been completed). All candidates must not be on Baseball's Ineligible List."

As for those figures on the Era Committee ballot for 2027, here's a quick rundown:

Alderson built a powerhouse and won a World Series as general manager of the Oakland A's. He later earned multiple playoff berths and a pennant as GM of the New York Mets.

One of the winningest managers of all time, Baker guided five different clubs to the playoffs and won three pennants and a World Series. His success in the dugout came after a long and distinguished playing career as an MLB outfielder.

Bochy as a manager led three different clubs to the postseason and is one of just six managers ever to win at least four World Series. Three of Bochy's rings came with the San Francisco Giants, and the final one came with the Texas Rangers in 2023.

Maddon won more than 1,300 games as a manager for three different franchises. He also won a pennant as manager of the Tampa Bay Rays, and in 2016, he led the Chicago Cubs to their first World Series title in more than a century.

After an 18-year playing career, Piniella racked up more than 1,800 wins as a big-league manager. He led three different clubs to the playoffs, won a World Series as manager of the 1990 Cincinnati Reds, and in 2001 helmed the Seattle Mariners to a record 116 wins during the regular season.

After filling a key role in the New York Yankees front office, Sabean joined the Giants as their general manager. Under his guidance, the Giants won the World Series in 2010, 2012, and 2014.

The only posthumous candidate on the ballot, Turner owned the Atlanta Braves for two decades. Along the way, he innovated the distribution of televised baseball games and oversaw a dynasty. Under Turner's stewardship, the Braves claimed 14 straight division titles and won the World Series in 1995.

A five-time All-Star and Gold Glove first baseman as a player, White after his playing days were over served as president of the National League. White was also the first Black play-by-play broadcaster in MLB history, and his leadership of the NL made him the first Black president of a major sports league.

The results of the committee vote will be announced on MLB Network at 8 p.m. ET on Sunday, Dec. 6. As with the BBWAA ballot, a candidate must be named on at least 75% of ballots in order to earn election. A 16-member committee will vote on the candidates.

The more traditional BBWAA ballot, in which candidates are voted on by writers and other media members, will be revealed on Nov. 16. Results of the 2027 BBWAA ballot will be announced in January, at which point we'll know the full Hall of Fame class for 2027.

#2706. Draymond Green gets first ejection of season after sparking Warriors-Suns scuffle

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Draymond Green made it to November (barely) before earning his first ejection of the 2026-27 NBA season.

On Monday night, Green took exception to getting knocked over by Phoenix Suns center Khaman Maluach posting up in transition and got up and tackled Maluach, wrapping him up with both arms and throwing him to the ground -- Maluach still made a basket for an and-1. Dillon Brooks then ran over to confront Green, which unsurprisingly led to a brief scuffle between the two and Green was eventually given two technical fouls and ejected in an eventual Warriors win.

Draymond Green was assessed a double technical on this play and was ejected. pic.twitter.com/uCmsTQxmcX

"I was just trying to de-escalate it," Brooks said. "He was just tweaking all game."

The ejection is Green's 31st of his career and he now has three technical fouls this season, tied for the most in the league. Once a player reaches 16 technicals in a season, it triggers an automatic one-game suspension.

Without Green, the Warriors surged back from a double-digit second-half deficit to get a 116-113 win thanks to Stephen Curry's heroics with 34 points and a huge game off the bench from Charles Bassey, who scored 19 points and pulled down eight rebounds in 22 minutes due to Green's absence.

Bassey's 19 points in 22 minutes off the bench on Monday night equals Green's 19 points in 159 minutes of play this season. Green does lead the Warriors in assists (6.3 per game), and the offense hums around him with Curry and rookie star Yaxel Lendeborg combining for more than 50 points per game.

With the win, Golden State improved to 5-3 on the season and now sits in seventh in the Western Conference standings early in the season as the Warriors try to claw their way back to the playoffs for the first time in three seasons.
